occasion.name: Nativity of the Lord - Proper II

notes.text: Day nor night — There shall be a vigilant and industrious ministry. Ye - That is, are his servants. And here especially are meant his servants in ordinary, his remembrancers, such as put God in mind of his promise, and such as make the Lord to be remembered, putting his people in mind of him.

A praise — By sending the Messiah, and those labourers into his vineyard, whereby the church may be established, and settled on sure foundations, and so become a matter of praise to God. All the nations shall praise him for her.
But — Thou shalt not sow, and another reap, as formerly. Courts - In my courts: holiness being put for God himself.

Go through — It is doubled by way of emphasis. Go meet the Gentiles, whom God purposes to bring into the church. Prepare - Let them not have any obstructions in their way. Stones - That there be no stumbling-stone, or offense in their way. Standard - An allusion to soldiers, that set up their standard that the army may know where to repair from all quarters.

Zion — To Jerusalem, or the church. Thy salvation - Thy saviour. Reward - The reward due to the work. Christ's victory over his enemies, ver. 1-6. and mercy towards his church: in judgment remembering mercy, ver. 7-14. The church's prayer and complaint in faith, ver. 15-19.

glossa.text: *Upon thy walls.* ((ID.)) The apostles, the preachers, who fortify the Church, whose guardians are the angels. Whence: *All are ministering spirits, sent for their sakes who receive the inheritance of salvation ((Hebr. I))* . Or the walls of the Churches are the disciples of the apostles, whose guardians are the apostles themselves.
*Till he establish Jerusalem.* Which is, either that she herself, spread far and wide, be praised everywhere, or that she everywhere praise her Creator always.

*He hath sworn* by the Son, namely, who is the power of God and the wisdom of God. *In his right hand.* In the Son. Whence: *Thou hast made all things in wisdom ((Psal. CIII))*, who is both the arm and the strength of the Father: Whence, *All things were made by him ((Joan. I))*. *If I will give thy wheat.* The wheat of the Jews and their wine I have often given to their enemies, as is read in the book of Judges ((Judic. VI)): that in the time of harvest the Madianites used to rush in and gather their crops. And when they were led away captive, Samaritans were put in their place to eat their harvests. But in this place he understands the food of the Church, the virtues and good works, the body and blood of Christ. That is, the praises and the works which thou hadst spent upon idols, the demons used to eat. But after the coming of the Son the Lord was delighted in them. The wheat, therefore, and the wine, the food (namely of the Jews), signified the body and blood of Christ. Whence, *My flesh is meat indeed, and my blood is drink indeed ((Joan. VI))*. This is not taken today by heretics, pagans, Jews, the enemies of the Church.

*Through the gates.* The ministers of the Church, who bring others in. Or the virtues, which lead into heaven, as it were from virtue to virtue. *Make the way plain.* By taking away scandals; by remitting sins in baptism. *Choose ye.* Or, cast ye forth, according to the Septuagint, which is: take away the hardness of unbelief from the hearts of men; or, the reprobate and the hard, from the fellowship of the faithful.

*Say ye to the daughter of Sion.* Namely to the primitive Church, which was first out of the Jews: whence, *The sons of my mother have fought against me ((Cant. I))*. Or according to that: *But as many as received him ((Joan. I))*, etc.

*And they shall call him,* saying: You are the holy people, you are the redeemed of the Lord God . For so certain codices have it.

notes.text: Isles — The Gentile nations, as this word, used Isaiah xlii, 4, is expounded, Matt. xii, 21.
Darkness — A dark cloud doth encompass him.
Heavens — The angels, yea God himself from heaven.
Confounded — Let them be ashamed of their folly. Gods - All you whom the Gentiles have made the objects of their worship.
Zion — Thy people dwelling in Zion or Jerusalem, to whom Christ came. Heard - The fame of thy judgments, and the setting up the kingdom of the Messiah.
Light — Joy and happiness. Sown - Is laid up for them. This psalm sets forth the glory of the Redeemer, ver. 1-3. And the joy of the redeemed, ver. 4-9. A psalm.

glossa.text:
*The Lord hath reigned.* ((CASS.)) The prophet, seeing the superstitions of the world abound before the resurrection of Christ, sets against them: *The Lord hath reigned.* ((AUG.)) Who then is another to be worshipped? as it were, none; thereupon:

*Let the earth rejoice.* What remains to the idols? As it were, nothing.

*The islands.* The Churches of the whole world. *Many.* Not all, because of the assemblies of the heretics.

((CASS.)) Thereupon he tells what manner of Lord he is in the first coming.

*Clouds and darkness.* To the wicked, who are blind, he is cloudy and dark, to whom he shines with no brightness; but to the good, *Justice and judgment.* They who are corrected are his seat. Before his coming *fire shall go before,* because the wicked, kindled with wrath at the preaching of the prophets, took counsel of their slaying, and were inflamed unto indignation round about, because they were many, whereas the preachers were few.
*Fire shall go before him,* etc. ((AUG.)) As it were, they who are corrected are the seat of God, etc., *as far as* if they are wicked, unto consuming; if good, unto repairing.
*His lightnings have shone forth.* ((ID.)) The clouds grew cheap in their human form, but a wondrous brightness appeared in their words or deeds, and thereupon the earth was moved.
*They flowed down.* ((ID.)) Even if the pagan does not believe just now, yet he is overcome.
*Let them be confounded.* This has now been done. ((AUG.)) For idolatry now ceases. And let them blush who adore stones, because they are dead.

*Adore ye.* ((ID.)) The adoration of the angels therefore ceases, but they adore. The evil angels themselves wish to be adored, the good adore, and do not suffer themselves to be adored. Or at least by this example let idolatry cease.

 *I have heard and she was glad.* ((CASS.)) Secondly, after the restoration of the land, an exultation of every kind, etc., *as far as* as the brethren rejoiced over Cornelius, whom Peter baptized. *And they rejoiced.* ((AUG.)) The apostles heard, who were brethren in Judaea, that the Gentiles had received the word of God, and they were glad and magnified God.
*The earth . . . the gods.* ((ID.)) By *the earth* and *the gods* understand sinners and just men. Or, he signifies that he rules over things earthly and things heavenly.

*The Lord keepeth.* ((AUG.)) If, when thou hast begun to hate the malignant, persecutions follow after, fear not, because the Lord keeps the souls of his saints, for the taking away of whom is the last kind of persecution.

notes.text: When the love of God appeared — By the light of his Spirit to our inmost soul.

Not by works — In this important passage the apostle presents us with a delightful view of our redemption. Herein we have,

1. The cause of it; not our works or righteousness, but "the kindness and love of God our saviour."

2. The effects; which are, (1.) Justification; "being justified," pardoned and accepted through the alone merits of Christ, not from any desert in us, but according to his own mercy, "by his grace," his free, unmerited goodness. (2.) Sanctification, expressed by the laver of regeneration, (that is, baptism, the thing signified, as well as the outward sign,) and the renewal of the Holy Ghost; which purifies the soul, as water cleanses the body, and renews it in the whole image of God.

3. The consummation of all; - that we might become heirs of eternal life, and live now in the joyful hope of it.

glossa.text: *Benignity,* etc. Through which he bestowed spiritual gifts upon us abundantly.

notes.text: That all the world should be enrolled — That all the inhabitants, male and female, of every town in the Roman empire, with their families and estates, should be registered.
When Cyrenius was governor of Syria — When Publius Sulpicius Quirinus governed the province of Syria, in which Judea was then included.

And while they were there, the days were fulfilled that she should be delivered — Mary seems not to have known that the child must have been born in Bethlehem, agreeably to the prophecy. But the providence of God took care for it.

She laid him in the manger — Perhaps it might rather be translated in the stall. They were lodged in the ox stall, fitted up on occasion of the great concourse, for poor guests. There was no room for them in the inn - Now also, there is seldom room for Christ in an inn. Matt. i, 25
To you — Shepherds; Israel; mankind.

Glory be to God in the highest; on earth peace; good will toward men — The shouts of the multitude are generally broken into short sentences. This rejoicing acclamation strongly represents the piety and benevolence of these heavenly spirits: as if they had said, Glory be to God in the highest heavens: let all the angelic legions resound his praises. For with the Redeemer's birth, peace, and all kind of happiness, come down to dwell on earth: yea, the overflowings of Divine good will and favour are now exercised toward men.
For all the things that they had heard — From Mary; as it was told them - By the angels.

glossa.text: *There went out a decree from Caesar. ((AUG., BED.))* Augustus reigned in peace for twelve years about the nativity of Christ, etc., *as far as* here first Judaea was made tributary to the Romans.

*The first. ((BEDA.))* Already at various times very many parts of the world are read to have been enrolled, but this is the first of those which took in the whole world; and it is a profession of minds, because no one is shut out. Or certainly it then first began, when Cyrinus was sent by Caesar into Syria, to be an assessor of patrimonies.

*Nazareth. ((ID.))* Daily the Lord is conceived in Nazareth, etc., *as far as* the insistence of the teacher who speaks avails nothing unless it has received the increase of help from above that it may be heard.

*And it came to pass.* The Lord willed to be conceived in one place and born in another, that he might the more easily escape the fury of the plotting Herod. The humility of Christ is commended, because he willed not only to be made flesh, but even to be born at that time in which, as soon as he was born, he should be made subject to Caesar's census for the sake of our deliverance.

*She wrapped him up in swaddling clothes.* He is clothed in mean cloths, that we might receive the robe of immortality. His hands and feet are bound fast, that our hands may be directed to working well, and our feet into the way of peace; he was made a little one, that we might be perfect.
*And there were shepherds. ((BEDA.))* The highest shepherd being born, the shepherds from the snares of the night, etc., *as far as* upon whom the divine grace flashes more abundantly.

*And behold an angel of the Lord. ((ID.))* The citizens of heaven bear witness to the Lord both as to be conceived, and as conceived, and as born, that they may both sufficiently instruct mortals and pay their own service to their author.

*An infant wrapped in swaddling clothes. ((ID.))* The infancy of the Saviour has been pressed home by frequent testimonies both of the angels and of the evangelists, that it may be fixed the more deeply in our minds what he was made for our sake: in which his humility is commended: *Because, whereas he was rich, he became poor for us, that by his own poverty he might enrich us ((II Cor))*.

*And on earth peace.* When by sinning we were strangers to God, the angels reckoned us strangers; but because we have known our king, the angels have recognized us as their own fellow citizens. And the angel fears to be adored by a human nature which he beholds in his own king.

*To men of good will. ((BEDA.))* Who receive Christ when born; not to those who at the hearing of his nativity were troubled and persecuted him. *There is no peace to the wicked, saith the Lord ((Isa. XLVIII))*.
*And they came with haste. ((BEDA.))* The presence of Christ is not to be sought with sloth, etc., *as far as* they will find him as it were in a manger.
*And seeing.* It is the vision or knowledge of God, and this alone is the life of men, that they should know the true Father, and that Jesus Christ, whom he sent, is one God.

*They wondered.* They wonder both at the mystery of the incarnation and at so great a testimony of shepherds, who did not know how to feign what they had heard, but with a simple eloquence proclaimed true things. But the Lord appointed not orators but fishermen to preach the Gospel. So too in the Old Testament he ordained shepherds as the messengers of his dispensation. Therefore the testimony of the shepherds is not to be lightly esteemed.

*And returning,* etc. ((BEDA.)) Thus spiritual shepherds, while others sleep, are borne up by contemplating heavenly things, etc., *as far as* when they say: *Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace to men of good will.*

echoes.text: I will sprinkle clean water on you, and you shall be clean: from all your filthiness, and from all your idols, will I cleanse you. I will also give you a new heart, and I will put a new spirit within you; and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you a heart of flesh. I will put my Spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and you shall keep my ordinances, and do them.
echoes.note: The new-covenant promise to sprinkle clean water for cleansing and to put a new spirit within stands directly behind the washing of regeneration and renewing by the Holy Spirit. The pairing of water-cleansing with Spirit-renewal is the structural template of Titus' soteriology.

echoes.text: “It will happen afterward, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh; and your sons and your daughters will prophesy. Your old men will dream dreams. Your young men will see visions. And also on the servants and on the handmaids in those days, I will pour out my Spirit.
echoes.note: The promise that God will pour out his Spirit on all flesh underlies the statement that he poured out the Spirit on us richly. The verb of outpouring is the prophetic signature for the eschatological gift of the Spirit appropriated here.

echoes.text: For I will pour water on him who is thirsty, and streams on the dry ground. I will pour my Spirit on your seed, and my blessing on your offspring:
echoes.note: I will pour water on the thirsty and my Spirit on your offspring fuses water and Spirit exactly as Titus fuses the washing with the renewing of the Holy Spirit. The double pouring of water and Spirit is the prophetic matrix for the regenerating bath.

echoes.text: neither will I hide my face any more from them; for I have poured out my Spirit on the house of Israel, says the Lord Yahweh.
echoes.note: God's pledge that I have poured out my Spirit on the house of Israel reinforces the outpouring language of verse 6. The prophetic image of lavish Spirit-effusion grounds Paul's emphasis on the Spirit poured out richly.

echoes.text: Purify me with hyssop, and I will be clean. Wash me, and I will be whiter than snow.
echoes.note: Purge me and I shall be clean, wash me and I shall be whiter than snow voices the cleansing-by-washing that Titus names the washing of regeneration. The penitential plea for inward purity prefigures the saving bath grounded in mercy, not works.

echoes.text: Create in me a clean heart, O God. Renew a right spirit within me.
echoes.note: Create in me a clean heart and renew a right spirit within me supplies the language of renewal by the Spirit. The Davidic prayer joins cleansing and inward renewing precisely as Titus joins washing and renewing of the Holy Spirit.

echoes.text: I will put my Spirit in you, and you shall live, and I will place you in your own land: and you shall know that I, Yahweh, have spoken it and performed it, says Yahweh.
echoes.note: I will put my Spirit in you and you shall live undergirds the link between Spirit-indwelling and the hope of eternal life in verse 7. The vivifying gift of the Spirit that raises the dead nation prefigures regeneration unto life.

echoes.text: Yahweh passed by before him, and proclaimed, “Yahweh! Yahweh, a merciful and gracious God, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness and truth,
echoes.note: The self-revelation of the LORD as merciful, gracious, and abounding in steadfast love stands behind the appearance of the kindness and love of God who saves according to his mercy. The grace-formula of Sinai is the theological ground for salvation not by works.

echoes.text: “For the unclean, they shall take of the ashes of the burning of the sin offering; and running water shall be poured into a vessel. A clean person shall take hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle it on the tent, on all the vessels, on the persons who were there, and on him who touched the bone, or the slain, or the dead, or the grave. The clean person shall sprinkle on the unclean on the third day, and on the seventh day. On the seventh day, he shall […]
echoes.note: The ritual sprinkling of the water of purification to cleanse defilement informs the cultic background of the washing of regeneration. The Mosaic lustration provides the ceremonial idiom later spiritualized into the saving bath.

echoes.text: I will make mention of the loving kindnesses of Yahweh and the praises of Yahweh, according to all that Yahweh has bestowed on us, and the great goodness toward the house of Israel, which he has bestowed on them according to his mercies, and according to the multitude of his loving kindnesses.
echoes.note: The recital of the LORD's lovingkindnesses and the multitude of his mercies frames God's saving action as kindness and love, echoed in the kindness of God our Savior and his love toward mankind. Salvation is grounded in covenant mercy rather than desert.

echoes.text: Israel, hope in Yahweh, for with Yahweh there is loving kindness. With him is abundant redemption.
echoes.note: With the LORD is steadfast love and plenteous redemption colors the claim that salvation rests on mercy and issues in justification by grace. The psalm's hope in abundant redemption parallels the hope of eternal life made the believer's inheritance.

echoes.text: It will happen that whoever will call on Yahweh’s name shall be saved; for in Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be those who escape, as Yahweh has said, and among the remnant, those whom Yahweh calls.
echoes.note: The promise that whoever calls on the name of the LORD shall be saved follows the Spirit-outpouring oracle and undergirds the language of being saved according to mercy. The Joel context links Spirit and salvation as Titus does.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: For to us a child is born. To us a son is given; and the government will be on his shoulders. His name will be called Wonderful, Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.
echoes.note: The angel announces a child born 'this day' who is 'Savior... Christ the Lord' bringing 'great joy' and 'peace,' the cluster of Isaiah's oracle of the child born to us, called the Prince of Peace, on whose shoulder the government rests. Coherence is exact (birth, joy, peace, Davidic rule) and the theme recurs across the infancy account, giving strong volume despite no formula quotation.

echoes.text: Now therefore you shall tell my servant David this, ‘Thus says Yahweh of Armies, “I took you from the sheep pen, from following the sheep, that you should be prince over my people, over Israel.
echoes.note: Shepherds first receive the Davidic birth announcement, fittingly because David was taken 'from following the sheep' to shepherd Israel. The motif of the shepherd-king frames the angel's proclamation of a 'Savior... in the city of David'; coherence is high, though the link is conceptual rather than quoted.

echoes.text: Yahweh’s glory settled on Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it six days. The seventh day he called to Moses out of the midst of the cloud.
echoes.note: 'The glory of the LORD shone around them' renders the Septuagintal doxa kyriou, the visible Sinai/tabernacle glory that settled and shone. Luke uses the technical theophany vocabulary, giving real volume; coherence is high as the kabod now attends the announcement of salvation.

echoes.text: You have multiplied the nation. You have increased their joy. They rejoice before you according to the joy in harvest, as men rejoice when they divide the plunder.
echoes.note: 'Good news of great joy' echoes Isaiah's 'they rejoice before you... as men rejoice when they divide the spoil,' the joy attending the breaking of the oppressor's yoke in the same Immanuel oracle that names the child. The joy-language strengthens the broader Isaiah 9 allusion in this pericope.

echoes.text: How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of him who brings good news, who publishes peace, who brings good news of good, who publishes salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns!”
echoes.note: The angel 'brings good news' (euangelizomai) of peace and salvation, the very verb-and-content of Isaiah's herald who publishes peace and announces 'your God reigns.' Septuagintal availability is direct and the salvation/peace coherence is strong; Luke universalizes it to 'all the people.'

echoes.text: You, tower of the flock, the hill of the daughter of Zion, to you it will come, yes, the former dominion will come, the kingdom of the daughter of Jerusalem.
echoes.note: The shepherds 'keeping watch over their flock' near Bethlehem evoke Micah's 'tower of the flock' (Migdal Eder), traditionally located by Bethlehem and read messianically as the place where kingship returns. Verbal contact is slight in Greek, so the echo is faint, but the Bethlehem-shepherd-king geography is thematically coherent.

echoes.text: Yahweh will give strength to his people. Yahweh will bless his people with peace.
echoes.note: The Gloria's 'on earth peace' set beside the heavenly host's praise recalls the psalm in which the LORD enthroned amid the heavenly beings 'gives strength to his people' and 'blesses his people with peace.' The host-of-heaven plus peace pairing is coherent though the verbal contact is thin, so it is a faint supporting echo.

echoes.text: One called to another, and said, “Holy, holy, holy, is Yahweh of Armies! The whole earth is full of his glory!”
echoes.note: The 'multitude of the heavenly army' crying 'Glory to God in the highest' resembles the seraphim antiphon 'Holy... the whole earth is full of his glory,' a heavenly liturgy proclaiming God's glory over the earth. The pattern (angelic chorus, glory, earth) is coherent though Luke's wording is independent.

echoes.text: Praise Yah! Praise Yahweh from the heavens! Praise him in the heights! Praise him, all his angels! Praise him, all his army!
echoes.note: 'Glory to God in the highest' with the angelic host praising parallels the psalm's call to 'praise him in the heights... praise him, all his hosts/angels.' The heights/host/praise vocabulary is coherent, supplying a plausible liturgical backdrop to the Gloria, though faint as direct source.

echoes.text: Then Samuel took the horn of oil, and anointed him in the midst of his brothers: and the Spirit of Yahweh came mightily on David from that day forward. So Samuel rose up, and went to Ramah.
echoes.note: Naming Jesus 'Savior... Christ (anointed) the Lord' in David's city recalls the anointing of David at Bethlehem when the Spirit rushed upon him. The christos-David-Bethlehem nexus is coherent within the chapter's Davidic frame, though no verbal echo is pressed.

echoes.text: His brothers envied him, but his father kept this saying in mind.
echoes.note: 'Mary kept all these sayings, pondering them in her heart' resembles Jacob who 'kept the saying in mind' after Joseph's dreams (LXX: dieterei to rhema). The verbal pattern (keeping/treasuring a rhema) is close and recurs at 2:51, giving recurrence, though the motif is also a general wisdom convention, so the specific source is contested.

echoes.text: Here is the end of the matter. As for me, Daniel, my thoughts much troubled me, and my face was changed in me: but I kept the matter in my heart.
echoes.note: Mary's treasuring the matter 'in her heart' parallels Daniel who 'kept the matter in my heart' (LXX) after a revelation he did not fully grasp. The apocalyptic reticence-and-treasuring motif coheres with Luke's portrayal of a not-yet-understood revelation, but the link is faint.

echoes.text: I will declare your name to my brothers. In the midst of the assembly, I will praise you.
echoes.note: The shepherds 'returned, glorifying and praising God' and publishing the saying recalls the psalmist's vow to 'declare your name to my brothers; in the midst of the assembly I will praise you.' The proclaim-and-praise pattern is coherent but generic, so a faint echo at best.

registers.label: Spare
lines: The shepherds said, Let us go and see this thing.
And they hurried to the manger.
They found the child, just as they were told.
And they could not keep silent.
You who felt forsaken, hear your new name.
Sought Out. Not Forsaken.
Come, let us worship with the shepherds.
Glory to God. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: The angels have gone back into heaven, and the shepherds are running — down the hill, through the dark streets, to see the thing the Lord has made known.
The Word became flesh and dwells among us.
They find him, just as they were told, a baby wrapped tight and lying in a manger, and they cannot keep the news in their mouths.
The Word became flesh and dwells among us.
You who have called yourself forsaken, abandoned, passed over — listen, for God is giving you a new name: Sought Out.
The Word became flesh and dwells among us.
Come with the shepherds, then, and go back as they did, praising God for all you have heard and seen.
The Word became flesh and dwells among us. Glory to God!

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: The shepherds hurry through the dark to see.
The Word became flesh and dwells among us.
They find the child and cannot stay silent.
The Word became flesh and dwells among us.
You who felt forsaken are now Sought Out.
The Word became flesh and dwells among us.
Come, let us worship and go telling it.
The Word became flesh and dwells among us. Glory to God!
